summary: This work introduces a Pareto-front optimization framework for periodic flux modulation of fluxonium qubits that simultaneously optimizes energy relaxation time $T_1$ and pure dephasing time $T_\phi$, revealing trade-offs between these coherence metrics at dynamical sweet spots. For realistic device parameters ($E_C/2\pi=1$ GHz, $E_L/2\pi=0.79$ GHz, $E_J/2\pi=4.43$ GHz), optimized waveforms achieve $T_\phi$ enhanced by factors of 3–5 compared to prior DSS schemes while maintaining $T_1$ in the 500–900 μs range, and the framework proves a fundamental upper bound on $T_1$ within the DSS regime under $\sigma_z$-coupled noise.
motivation: Existing dynamical sweet spot strategies suppress low-frequency flux noise sensitivity but suffer an inherent trade-off between $T_1$ and $T_\phi$ that limits coherence extension. The work asks whether simultaneous optimization of both coherence times is possible under general periodic flux control and what fundamental limits govern the maximum achievable values.
method: Multi-objective genetic algorithms (NSGA2, SPEA2, tDEA, ENS-MOEA/D, HypE) optimize Fourier coefficients of periodic flux modulation while computing decoherence rates from Floquet theory in the presence of 1/$f$ flux noise ($A_f=1.8\times10^{-6}$) and dielectric loss ($\tan(\delta_C)=1.1\times10^{-6}$); results are validated against 5-level full fluxonium Hamiltonians and exemplified by gate design using charge-drive control pulses superimposed on DSS backgrounds.
result: A 3–5 fold improvement in $T_\phi$ (reaching 7.4 ms at DSS-3) with $T_1\geq550$ μs is demonstrated; double-DSS points insensitive to both DC and AC flux achieve $T_\phi$ improvements of 215$\times$ over single-DSS at matched $T_1$; single-qubit X gates achieve $F_\mathrm{avg}=99.99\%$ with leakage $L_\mathrm{avg}=9.35\times10^{-6}$ in 11 ns, and two-qubit i-SWAP gates achieve $F_\mathrm{avg}=99.92\%$ with leakage $L_\mathrm{avg}=7.18\times10^{-4}$ in 34 ns (both validated at $N=12$ level truncation).
